The Philadelphia Phillies ’ need for right-handed offense is drawing attention early in free agency, with two established outfielders emerging as suggested additions to their lineup. Philadelphia finished last in OPS from right-handed hitters in 2026, according to MLB Network Radio. That ranking provides the backdrop for a discussion about strengthening the Phillies’ offense through the open market. The segment focused on players who finished the season with the Seattle Mariners and Chicago Cubs, respectively. Both now face qualifying-offer decisions that could determine whether they remain with those organizations for another year. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) MLB Network Radio shared host Mike Ferrin’s assessment Thursday on X, formerly Twitter, underscoring the connection between Philadelphia’s offensive shortcoming and available outfield talent. “Randy’s going to get paid, and he’s going to be a really good addition for somebody… The Phillies. Oh my God, the Phillies could use Randy Arozarena . Phillies could use Seiya Suzuki .” The #Phillies finished LAST in OPS from right-handed hitters in 2026. Does free agency have the fix? #RingTheBell 🔗 https://t.co/iXax8hx4iO pic.twitter.com/9uKiwk20cE — MLB Network Radio on SiriusXM (@MLBNetworkRadio) November 5, 2026 Arozarena, 31, hit .281 with a .381 on-base percentage, 26 home runs and 79 RBIs for the Mariners. He also stole 26 bases, contributing on the bases alongside his offensive production. Suzuki finished with a .270/.368/.473 slash line, 26 home runs and 86 RBIs across 143 regular-season games for Chicago. His on-base percentage and slugging percentage combined for an .841 OPS. The Mariners and Cubs extended one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offers to Arozarena and Suzuki on Monday. Each player has until November 17 to accept or decline. Acceptance would keep a player with his current team under that contract. Declining would preserve the opportunity to negotiate a different agreement, including a potential return to the same club. Ferrin’s comments present possible fits rather than establish contact between Philadelphia and either player. The clip does not identify an offer, contract demand or active negotiation at this early stage. For now, both players have qualifying offers pending, and the Phillies’ next outfield move remains unresolved. item.title: Don’t buy this hype: Why Georgia is in danger against Ole Miss
item.description: Week 10 of the college football season brings us seven matchups between ranked teams, including a critical SEC clash of titans between Georgia and Ole Miss. Reigning SEC champion Georgia has more breathing room than two-loss Ole Miss, but both need this to go their way to further impress the College Football Playoff committee. Georgia comes into the game as a favorite, but Ole Miss could have one decisive advantage on its home field if they can exploit it. Make Gunner Stockton Win Through the Air Sep 27, 2025; Athens, Georgia, USA; Georgia Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton (14) looks to pass against the Alabama Crimson Tide in the first half at Sanford Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Ole Miss enters Saturday’s matchup with a clear defensive objective: make Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton uncomfortable and force the Bulldogs to rely on their passing attack. The biggest question about the Georgia offense remains its aerial offense. It struggled against one of the worst secondaries in the SEC a week ago. Florida ranked 112th nationally in EPA per pass and 126th in passing success rate. But the Bulldogs managed just 101 passing yards in an otherwise dominant win. Disrupt the Timing The Rebels need to challenge Georgia’s receivers at the line of scrimmage and disrupt Stockton’s timing. Physical coverage can delay routes developing and force him to hold the football longer, giving Ole Miss’ defensive front additional time to generate pressure. Defensive tackle Will Echoles could be especially important. His ability to collapse the pocket and disrupt throwing lanes could prevent Stockton from comfortably working through his progressions. More: Predicting SEC football scores for Week 10’s biggest games Take Away the Easy Throws Ole Miss should prioritize limiting Georgia’s short and intermediate passing options. Forcing Stockton into difficult third-down situations would give the Rebels opportunities to disguise coverages, bring pressure, and potentially create turnovers. The goal shouldn’t necessarily be to gamble for interceptions. Instead, Ole Miss must make Georgia earn every completion and avoid allowing yards after the catch. Turn Pressure Into Mistakes Georgia’s offense becomes less predictable when it stays ahead of the chains. If Ole Miss can stop the run on early downs, it can force Stockton into obvious passing situations. Ultimately, Ole Miss doesn’t need to completely shut down Georgia’s passing game. It needs to disrupt its rhythm, eliminate easy completions, and force Stockton to make difficult decisions under pressure. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Why Chiefs WR Rashee Rice reportedly filed for bankruptcy after legal battles
item.description: Why Chiefs WR Rashee Rice reportedly filed for bankruptcy after legal battles originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy on Wednesday, court documents showed, per WFAA. Rice reportedly claimed over $3 million in debts in the filing, which came in the Northern District of Texas bankruptcy court. A majority of those listed debts, per ESPN , were tied to "varying plaintiffs suing him in civil litigation that have either been settled or are awaiting trial." Here's what's known about Rice filing for bankruptcy. MORE: NFL trade deadline predictions, projected landing spots Chiefs WR Rashee Rice files for bankruptcy According to WFAA, Rice filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy on Nov. 4, court documents showed, listing his estimated assets to be worth "between $500,000 and $1 million," and his estimated liabilities between "$1 million to $10 million." Rice listed various assets in the filing, including his Super Bowl 53 ring, a Mercedes-Benz, and NFL apparel, per WFAA. ESPN also reported that federal court records showed Rice claimed "more than $3.45 million in debts" in the filing, including more than $2.1 million of which is tied to civil lawsuits that have either been settled or are awaiting trial. The Chiefs wide receiver has been involved in multiple lawsuits tied to his role in a high-speed car crash in Dallas in 2024, along with an ex-girlfriend alleging he repeatedly assaulted her from 2023 to 2025, per ESPN . In July 2025, Rice pleaded guilty to two third-degree felonies in connection with the Dallas car crash incident. He served 30 days in a Dallas County jail in June 2026 after reportedly violating his probation terms after testing positive for THC. According to ESPN, in the bankruptcy filing, Rice claimed to have a total of $677,054 in personal assets, with his largest creditor owed $979,837 as part of a civil settlement related to the 2024 car crash. Rice is also still disputing potential debts from the civil lawsuits, including "a combined $700,000 in lawsuits filed by 2024 crash victims and $200,000 as part of the alleged assault suit," per ESPN. Rice's Super Bowl ring was also reportedly used as collateral with his attorney in the pending civil cases, valued at $160,000. Rice, 26, is in the final year of his rookie contract with Kansas City in 2026. According to Spotrac , he signed a four-year, $6.4 million deal with the Chiefs in 2023, set to hit free agency this upcoming offseason. Over five games this season, Rice has posted 20 catches for 243 yards and two touchdowns. MORE: Who needs Jonathan Taylor the most?

item.title: Chiefs sign wide receiver Bub Means to the practice squad
item.description: (Photo by Derick E. Hingle/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to Thursday’s NFL Transactions Report, the Kansas City Chiefs have added another receiver to their practice squad. Bub Means, a fifth-round pick of the New Orleans Saints in the 2024 NFL Draft, was listed as a practice-squad transaction for the Chiefs a day after he tried out for a spot. He was one of nine players Kansas City hosted for tryouts on Wednesday. The Chiefs also signed wide receiver Jacob De Jesus, who spent time with the team this offseason. Means has not played in a regular-season game since his rookie year in New Orleans in 2024, when he appeared in seven games and produced 118 yards and seven first downs over nine receptions. All of his production came in a three-game stretch, Weeks 6-8 of that rookie campaign. He spent 68% of his snaps as an outside receiver during that period with an average depth of target of 12 yards. Rattler to Bub Means. Both of their first TD's pic.twitter.com/MqVkjiur7c — Saints Film Room (@SaintsFilmRoom) October 13, 2024 Means was cut after the preseason this year, then spent time on the Cleveland Browns ‘ practice squad this season. Before he was a fifth-round selection out of the University of Pittsburgh, Means racked up 1,552 yards and 10 touchdowns over two seasons at Pitt and one prior at Louisiana Tech. Means was originally a three-star high school recruit who enrolled at the University of Tennessee. During his last year in college, 42% of Means’ targets were 20 or more yards downfield; he caught 10 passes for 395 yards and five touchdowns on deep throws in 2023. The 25-year-old joins Justin Watson and Jacob De Jesus to form a trio of practice-squad receivers for the Chiefs to call up; Andrew Armstrong was signed to the 53-man roster from the practice squad a couple of weeks ago.

item.title: ‘You want to be shaken and brought back to earth’: HC Mike Brown addresses Knicks poor start
item.description: Jun 5, 2026; San Antonio, Texas, USA; New York Knicks head coach Mike Brown speaks with the media after the game between the Spurs and the Knicks in game two of the 2026 NBA Finals at Frost Bank Center. Mandatory Credit: Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images The New York Knicks haven’t had the start to the season they expected, and the reigning champs may have celebrated too hard during the summer. But head coach Mike Brown isn’t worried about his team’s 3-4 start; rather, he’s “a little excited” about their current struggles. On Monday, the Knicks beat the Brooklyn Nets, defeating their neighbors across the bridge 103-90. The team has been off to a slow start, losing its first three games of the season and beginning its rivalry with the Philadelphia 76ers 0-2. The Nets looked competitive early, trailing just 51-44 at halftime, and they took a 79-75 lead into the fourth quarter after a 35-point third. But the defending champs rallied in the fourth quarter, as they are known to do, outscoring Brooklyn 28-11 to seal the deal. The next day, Brown was asked by a reporter, “Are you happy with the starts? Do you think the starts need to get better?” in reference to the team’s energy out of the gate. “Everything can get better,” Brown answered, via SNY Knicks on X . “Am I happy with it? I’m not pissed about the starts or upset about the starts. I’m actually — there’s a part of me… I’m a little excited that we’re struggling a little bit. Because I want to see if we, right now, can figure it out — not figure it out in 10 games and take off and win the last 72, cause that ain’t happening; we’re still going to go through our lulls. But when you go through the off-season that we just went through, where everybody celebrates you the way this lovely city did, and the fans of the New York Knicks did, you want to be shaken and brought back to earth right away when the season starts, because that grounds you; everybody, starting with me on down, obviously, is human, and sometimes you can get a little full of yourself. “So if you hit some challenges or some adversity early on, it helps you refocus a little bit quicker, which can help you get on track the right way sooner. Because right now we could be winning games, but it could be false reality. I said it before: new season, new challenges. Right now, because we’re not playing our best basketball, we’re seeing some of the challenges that we need to work on, and we’re either going to work on them and embrace them, or we’re going to fold, and I don’t think this team has any folding in them, so I’m okay with this.” Finals MVP Jalen Brunson has shown glimpses of last season but hasn’t fully fallen into his normal role just yet either. item.title: Dodgers Have 2 Intriguing Trade Targets as Marlins Make Infielders Available
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers’ biggest position of need is second base if they want to upgrade offensively on what they have. Tommy Edman is one option at second, along with infield prospect Alex Freeland and possibly even Hyeseong Kim. If the Dodgers want another option, someone who had an impressive 2026 season or a better track record than either Kim or Freeland, the Miami Marlins have a pair of infielders who are reportedly available. Aug 16, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Miami Marlins shortstop Otto Lopez (6) high fives second baseman Xavier Edwards (9) after the victory over the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park. Mandatory Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images Otto Lopez, shortstop, and Xavier Edwards, second baseman, are two players who, according to Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald , may be traded for “a lot” in exchange. Both Lopez and Edwards have three years of arbitration control, so they are under control until 2030. The Marlins don’t need either of them urgently, but it is an opportunity for at least the Dodgers to explore . Here is what the pair offers: Xavier Edwards Edwards is a multi-positional defender who can play second base and shortstop. His defense declined in 2026 after being above average. Still, he is a walking specialist, with an 11.4% walk rate; he avoids strikeouts (13.9%) and puts the ball in play, but doesn’t hit it hard. More importantly, he’s fast and ranks as an elite base-runner, with at least 21 SBs over the last three years. The Dodgers need speed, and Edwards’s .360 OBP means his speed shows up on the bases. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dodgers Nation (@dodgersnation) Otto Lopez Lopez is likely the more expensive player, given how amazing his 2026 was. He put up a 5.9 fWAR season, with an above-average hitting season. Lopez slashed .305/.349/.437 with just 11 home runs, but drove in 94 runs, stole 34 bases, and drove in 71 runs. Sep 23, 2025; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Miami Marlins shortstop Xavier Edwards (9) and second base Otto Lopez (6) celebrate win against the Philadelphia Phillies at Citizens Bank Park. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images It was far and away his best offensive year, since he struggled to get much going before. He is strictly a contact specialist who is a master at putting the ball in play, even if it means a weak walk rate of 5.8%. However, he also plays elite defense, with three straight years as one of the league’s best infielders. Lopez can slot in at either second base or shortstop, and he plays them at a high level. Who should the Dodgers target? Out of the pair, Edwards makes the most sense, since he is likely to cost a bit less and has a more stable track record. Lopez has only one year of hitting at the level he produced in 2026, and for what the Marlins may ask, he may need another season of similar production to warrant that many prospects.

The Indianapolis Colts have a lot of decisions to make with regard to which players they want to trade and which ones they want to keep. Running back Jonathan Taylor will be the toughest choice of all and a surprise team has now entered the trade buzz conversation as Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk speculated the San Francisco 49ers might have interest in Taylor. This would be a jarring and shocking move for a number of reasons. First off, the 49ers already have a star running back in Christian McCaffrey. item.title: Luke Fahey’s ‘one hundred percent’ answer raises stakes for Ohio State against Oregon
item.description: Luke Fahey’s first public comments as the Ohio State Buckeyes’ starting quarterback came Thursday on Ryan Day’s radio show on 97.1 The Fan, ahead of Saturday’s home game against the Oregon Ducks. The true freshman had not been made available to beat reporters this season, so the show was the first time fans heard him describe how the job landed on him. Fahey was asked about taking the next step against Oregon, and he also walked through the stretch between Julian Sayin’s injury at the Indiana Hoosiers on Oct. 17 and the trip to the USC Trojans. Eleven Warriors reported that he also talked about his dream of being a starter and his desire to improve. Ohio State Buckeyes quarterback Luke Fahey (13) and quarterback Tavien St. Clair (9) warm up prior to the NCAA football game against the Texas Longhorns at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin, Texas on Sept. 12, 2026. “One hundred percent. I think after the first start, I will hopefully start to settle down. That first week was definitely rough, but I’m excited to move forward. … My mind was going in all kinds of different places, so I was thinking about a lot of different things. Before I knew it, it was one week before we were playing, and then before I knew it, we were taking off [for California]. It happened pretty quick,” Fahey said , Bill Rabinowitz reported. How rough was Luke Fahey’s first start against USC? The roughness he described was mostly in the days before kickoff, and the box score was kinder. Fahey went 21 of 38 for 260 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions in the 30-18 loss, and several big drops hurt that line. Ohio State piled up 464 total yards and still settled for three field goals on its first five drives, with 11 penalties along the way. Its only touchdown came with 2:12 left. Day stayed with Fahey over Tavien St. Clair after both took first-team reps during the bye week, and he put much of the USC result on the people around Fahey. “There’s things to build on there for sure. But we’ve got to do a better job around him, helping him out as a young player,” Day said Tuesday. Ryan Day Credits James Laurinaitis After Historic Top-10 Linebacker Draft Milestone (Imagn Images) Why Ohio State needs Fahey settled in right now At 6-2, the Buckeyes have little room left for another loss, and Day said on Thursday’s show that they are “starting the playoff season right now.” He also said Sayin won’t return in the next month, which covers a regular season that ends against the Michigan Wolverines on Nov. 28. Oregon comes in at 5-3, allowing 208.0 passing yards per game. Fahey will make his first start at Ohio Stadium at 3:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, this time with a week of preparation as the announced starter. item.description: Mar 10, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Golden State Warriors forward Draymond Green (23) during overtime against the Chicago Bulls at Chase Center. Mandatory Credit: Bob Kupbens-Imagn Images In Monday night’s matchup between the Golden State Warriors and the Phoenix Suns, veteran forward Draymond Green was ejected after playing only 17 minutes for the Warriors. With the regular season only eight games old, media critics have already begun to ask whether he is needed or if he is in the way of another championship. Early in the third quarter, Green collided with Suns center Khaman Maluach in the paint and was knocked over. Green responded by tackling Maluach to the ground after what seemed like an accidental encounter. The referee immediately assessed Green a technical, but the situation escalated further as Suns forward Dillon Brooks became involved in defense of his teammate. Green was ultimately ejected after a scuffle with Brooks that both sides had to break up, another ejection to add to his already extensive list throughout his career with the Warriors. On Tuesday, ESPN’s First Take panel questioned Green’s contribution as he enters his 15th season with the team and has shown a decline in play. “Could Draymond end up being a detriment to the Warriors and their aspirations this season?” asked First Take host Shae Cornette. “Hell yeah, listen, when was the last time we discussed Draymond Green and brought up him as far as his basketball and not fighting?” First Take analyst Kendrick Perkins said. “At some point, he has to deliver on the floor, and when you look at the start of this season, Draymond Green has been nonexistent. He has done absolutely nothing for the Golden State Warriors; to me, he has been a liability more than an asset.” Perkins supported his claim by pointing out the Warriors’ newly acquired talent in rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, who has had a remarkable start to the season. The former Boston Celtic noted the brotherhood between star guard Stephen Curry and Green but insisted it would soon fade or even be replaced if Green’s antics don’t stop. “At some point we have to stop giving Draymond a pass and start to say, ‘Hey man, when are you going to start producing on the floor?’ and I know he’s not known for scoring, but the man is averaging three points, shooting 38% from the field and about 28% from the three-point line. That is unacceptable for a guy that’s getting paid the amount of money that Draymond Green is getting paid,” Perkins added. Green’s career has been marked by physical altercations, flagrant fouls, and general unsportsmanlike conduct, resulting in multiple suspensions over the last 15 years. But with the Warriors’ days coming to an eventual end soon, how long can Green get away with on-court distractions that hinder playoff chances?
